source_spans.locator: Nature Neuroscience 9(11), Advance Online Publication PDF p.1 / final p.1432, abstract and Results opening: variable population responses encode probability distributions over the stimulus

Nature Neuroscience 9(11), Advance Online Publication PDF p.2 / final p.1433, simple cue-integration derivation: conditional independence, Gaussian case, posterior mean/variance, and exact population-code summation under the stated assumptions

Nature Neuroscience 9(11), Advance Online Publication PDF pp.2-3 / final pp.1433-1434, general theory: Poisson-like exponential-family conditions, common h(s) requirement for direct addition, and common-basis condition for Bayes-optimal weighted linear combinations

conditions: the two cue observations are conditionally independent given the underlying stimulus for the cue-combination factorization

population responses obey the source's Poisson-like exponential-family form with the gain/covariance condition required by equations (4)-(5); direct neuron-by-neuron addition additionally requires the same h(s) structure across input layers and the simple derivation uses a flat prior
when input h_k(s) functions differ, Bayes-optimal weighted linear combinations require their components to be drawn from a common basis set
task: combine uncertain cues about an underlying stimulus variable
temporal_scope: single-trial population responses and their cue-combined output; no cross-trial temporal process is required by this target claim

nodes.description: first noisy population response associated with one cue
second noisy population response associated with another cue
probability distribution over the latent stimulus encoded by the first population response
probability distribution over the latent stimulus encoded by the second population response
source-explicit internal computation consisting of addition or a weighted linear combination of the input population activities
output population produced by the linear population computation
cue-combined probability distribution over the latent stimulus encoded by the output population
the Bayesian cue-combination posterior required by the source; in the Gaussian case equations (2) and (3) specify both posterior mean and posterior variance

relations.description: the first variable population response specifies a probability distribution over the latent stimulus
the second variable population response specifies another probability distribution over the latent stimulus
the source-explicit linear computation combines the two input population activities into an output population; this is a computational operation, not an experimental intervention
the output population activity encodes the cue-combined probability distribution
under the declared Poisson-like and cue-factorization conditions, direct addition or the permitted weighted linear combination yields the Bayesian cue-combination distribution
